summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with inoperable cholangiocarcinoma and a history of recurrent biliary infections, was admitted for progressive fatigue and weakness. Initial workup showed no active infection, with negative blood and urine cultures and only mixed flora in bile. Imaging revealed stable disease but a new L3 vertebral lesion concerning for metastasis, prompting a CT-guided biopsy. He was treated empirically with meropenem for suspected cholangitis, but symptoms did not improve, leading to discontinuation. Iron studies confirmed iron deficiency, and he received two doses of IV ferric gluconate. His pancytopenia worsened, likely due to chronic Bactrim and underlying disease. The portal vein thrombus resolved, but apixaban was continued per oncology. Anxiety and insomnia were managed with Ativan, which he continued at discharge. He was discharged home with services, pending biopsy results, on his baseline regimen including Bactrim, with follow-up for oncology and CBC monitoring.
